pr_title: fix(apt_repository): Detect changes to expiration in key
pr_body:
This makes it so that the apt keys are updated if the expiration of a key is updated without changing the fingerprint.

See: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-cookbooks/cookbook-gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/37/diffs#35cd6a49d9e22469db42af7a30c5f3a76487e3c7
Fixes: #13308

issue_context.title: apt_repository won't add a key if the expiration date has changed
issue_context.body:
## Description

We noticed that after extending our GPG key (https://about.gitlab.com/blog/2021/06/28/package-key-extension/) that `apt_repository` never added the newly-extended key.

## Chef Version

We use v14.13.11, but this bug still applies to `master`.

## Platform Version

Linux 20.04.

## Replication Case

1. Create a GPG key.
2. Use `apt_repository` with `key`.
3. Extend the key via instructions in https://makandracards.com/makandra-orga/13644-what-to-do-when-your-gpg-pgp-key-expires.
4. Run `chef-client` again.

## Client Output

Notice that the `apt-key add` step was skipped, even though the `remote_file` was updated properly:

```
Recipe: cookbook-gitlab-runner::runner_install
  * apt_repository[gitlab-runner] action add
    * remote_file[/var/chef/cache/https___packages_gitlab_com_runner_gitlab-runner_gpgkey] action create (up to date)
    * execute[apt-key add /var/chef/cache/https___packages_gitlab_com_runner_gitlab-runner_gpgkey] action run (skipped due to not_if)
    * execute[apt-cache gencaches] action nothing (skipped due to action :nothing)
    * apt_update[gitlab-runner] action nothing (skipped due to action :nothing)
    * file[/etc/apt/sources.list.d/gitlab-runner.list] action create (up to date)
     (up to date)
```

This resulted in a failure in the `apt install` since the repository had an expired key:

```
  * apt_package[gitlab-runner] action install

    ================================================================================
    Error executing action `install` on resource 'apt_package[gitlab-runner]'
    ================================================================================

    Mixlib::ShellOut::ShellCommandFailed
    ------------------------------------
    Expected process to exit with [0], but received '100'
    ---- Begin output of ["apt-get", "-q", "-y", "--allow-downgrades", "-o", "Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef", "-o", "Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold", "--force-yes", "install", "gitlab-runner=14.10.1"] ----
    STDOUT: Reading package lists...
    Building dependency tree...
    Reading state information...
    STDERR: E: Version '14.10.1' for 'gitlab-runner' was not found
    ---- End output of ["apt-get", "-q", "-y", "--allow-downgrades", "-o", "Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef", "-o", "Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold", "--force-yes", "install", "gitlab-runner=14.10.1"] ----
    Ran ["apt-get", "-q", "-y", "--allow-downgrades", "-o", "Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef", "-o", "Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold", "--force-yes", "install", "gitlab-runner=14.10.1"] returned 100
```

## Proposed solution

Currently `apt_repository` determines if a key needs to be added if the fingerprint isn't listed in the key list, but if a key expiration date is extended, the fingerprint does NOT change.

In https://gitlab.com/gitlab-cookbooks/cookbook-gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/37/diffs, we created a custom resource that changes the implementation of `no_new_keys?` to use the `pub` lines (https://github.com/gpg/gnupg/blob/25ae80b8eb6e9011049d76440ad7d250c1d02f7c/g10/keylist.c#L1570-L1577) instead of the `fpr` lines:

```ruby
      LIST_APT_KEY_PUBLIC_KEYS = %w[apt-key adv --list-public-keys --with-colons].freeze

      def no_new_keys?(file)
        # Now we are using the option --with-colons that works across old os versions
        # as well as the latest (16.10). This for both `apt-key` and `gpg` commands
        installed_keys = extract_public_keys_from_cmd(*LIST_APT_KEY_PUBLIC_KEYS)
        proposed_keys = extract_public_keys_from_cmd('gpg', '--with-colons', file)
        (installed_keys & proposed_keys).sort == proposed_keys.sort
      end

      def extract_public_keys_from_cmd(*cmd)
        so = shell_out(*cmd)
        # Sample output
        # pub:e:4096:1:14219A96E15E78F4:2015-04-17:2020-04-15::-:GitLab B.V. (package repository signing key) <packages@gitlab.com>::sc:
        # pub:-:4096:1:3F01618A51312F3F:2020-03-02:2024-03-01::-:GitLab B.V. (package repository signing key) <packages@gitlab.com>::scESC:
        #
        # Newer gpg versions use UNIX timestamps instead of the date.
        so.stdout.split(/\n/).map do |t|
          z = t.match(/(^pub:.?:\d*:\d*:\w*:[\d-]*:[\d-]*):/)
          z[1] if z
        end.compact
      end
```
comments: I think that I just ran into this with an update to the expiration for the keys used to sign the yarn PPA.

review_comments: Is `extract_fingerprints_from_cmd` deprecated by these changes? If so, would recommend removing it.
It is still used in `install_key_from_keyserver`. I'm not sure if it could be removed from that though.
